To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
salt activation of the ATPase in the roots of the halophytes Atriplex num-mularia and Mesembryanthemum crystallinum occurs at low pH and low concentrations of NaCl or KCl.
the NaCl-stimulated ATPases in membranes isolated from roots of A. nummularia and P. sativum are different in their response to salt.
The salt-activated ATPases of Atriplex and Pisum are different in their response to salt activation and inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of NaCl on the activity of ATPase from roots and leaves of Atriplex, a salt-tolerant plant.
the effects of NaCl on the activity of ATPase in the roots of Atripex nummularia and Pisum sativurn.
the mechanism of salt tolerance in Atriplex nummularia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the salt-activated ATPases from Atriplex numnularia and Pisum sativurn show similar characteristics in terms of pH optima, salt concentrations and salt types required for activation, and the salt concentration required to produce a half-maximal response.
the salt-activated ATPases of halophytes are more resistant to inhibition than those of glycophytes.
the salt-activation and salt-inhibition of ATPases from Atriplex num-mularia roots are not the result of a single process but are due to at least two different mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the salt-stimulated ATPases in Atriplex roots are insensitive to inhibition by salt, but are susceptible to salt inhibition in the MgATPases.
the salt activation and inhibition of Atriplex root plasma membrane ATPase are not due to the presence or absence of monovalent salts.
the salt-stimulated ATPases of both species showed a similar pattern of activation at the optimum pH but that the Atriplex enzyme was less sensitive to inhibition by high salt.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the salt activation of ATPase activity is a pH-dependent process.
salt activation and inhibition of ATPase activity are not necessarily related phenomena, and that salt stimulation of the ATPase is a complex process involving several components.
